## A — Exam authority for the no-passing zones, roundabouts, diverging diamonds and parking section (Arizona Class D operator license, written test)
Issuer: the Arizona Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Division (ADOT MVD) provides this manual as its guide to Arizona traffic laws and to obtaining a driver license or identification card [A05].
Source document: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, whose contents page carries the line Revised September 2026 [A03].
Purpose: the manual explains Arizona motor vehicle laws without technical language to help readers obtain a driver license or instruction permit, and refers to Arizona Revised Statutes Title 28 for the most current law [A03].
Written test: MVD issues an Arizona instruction permit only after the applicant passes the Division written test; commercial learner permits are excluded from this rule [A01].
Practice: the manual sends applicants to the MVD website to practice the written test [A02].
Road test link: before a road test, applicants must show they understand the meaning of Arizona traffic signs [A04].
Question count: not stated anywhere in the manual (verify AZ-PARK-A-COUNT).
Passing standard: not stated anywhere in the manual, so no threshold is shown to learners (verify AZ-PARK-A-PASS).
Item format and time limit: neither is stated in the manual (verify AZ-PARK-A-FORMAT; verify AZ-PARK-A-TIME).
Edition currency: the issuer web page could not be observed in this pass, so the current-edition status of the snapshot stays open (verify AZ-PARK-A-EDITION).
This section feeds the written test: the no-passing distances, the roundabout yield and speed rules, accessible-parking use and the hill-parking wheel positions are rules the manual sets for every driver before the written test.
Practice quizzes in this product follow the learning-loop mastery policy, which is a product rule and not an official exam threshold.

corpus_stability.reason: The Arizona Driver License Manual carries one revision line on its contents page (Revised September 2026) and points to Arizona Revised Statutes Title 28 for current law; nothing in the selected pages signals more than one rewrite per year.

verification_debt.claim_text: The Arizona Driver License Manual states no question count for the written test; an official ADOT MVD source is required before any count is shown.
The Arizona Driver License Manual states no passing score for the written test; no threshold may be shown to learners until an official ADOT MVD page states it.
The item format of the Arizona written test (multiple choice or otherwise) is not stated in the manual.
The Arizona Driver License Manual states no time limit for the written test.
The ADOT MVD issuer page for the manual returned a bot challenge during intake, so the snapshot edition (Revised September 2026, contents page) has not been confirmed as current on the issuer site.
